quote: When we gather together in the moonlit village ground it is not because of the moon. Every man can see it in his own compound. We come together because it is good for kinsmen to do so.
source: Chinua Achebe, Things Fall Apart, chapter 19, the farewell feast in Mbanta (an elder of the umunna) (William Heinemann, 1958)
speaker: one of the oldest members of the umunna
note: The wording is exact and the chapter is right. The page reference to the Penguin Modern Classics printing of 2001 could not be checked against a copy, so it is dropped and the first edition is named instead. The feast is the one Okonkwo gives his mother’s kinsmen in Mbanta at the end of his exile.

evidence.edition: Things Fall Apart, chapter 19; first published by William Heinemann in 1958, written in English so no translator

reason: The passage is genuine, in the named chapter, and spoken by one of the oldest members of the umunna as the proposal says. Only the unverified page and edition needed correcting.
